messages:
devon: Heads-up — canary GPU pool in eu-west-3 started seeing a cluster of device resets right after the kernel 6.1.21 + nvidia-driver 540.12 rollout. ~8 resets in 12m, nodes circling reprovision. sample dmesg shows 'GPU reset (reason 31) / PCR: 0x1f3'.
cameron: copying logs, pausing further driver rollouts to other regions. pinging @eng-infra oncall.
depon-bot: (automated) Canary deployment 2025-09-12T09:40: rolling hold activated for pool: canary-eu-west-3.
isabel: are these XID codes or new vendor error strings? send me a gcore + nvidia-smi output from one affected host.
maria: I grabbed one: attached snippet below. looks like NVLINK errors + 'pci_bus_error: severity=Uncorrected (PCIe)'.
maria: ```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ERRORS
GPU 0: Volatile Device Error: 3
GPU 0: Xid (or reset reason): 0x1f3
# dmesg | tail -n50
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: GPU PCI AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error
[ 1234.567893] pcieport 0000:64:00.0: bridge error: logged Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error
```
devon: interesting — we've not seen 0x1f3 in our fleet before. can't reproduce on local test harness. only in canary on physical hosts.
cameron: I've paused canary autoscale and marked nodes as unschedulable. collecting perf counters and nvml traces. can someone run the nv-hostmgr debug on one node?
isabel: running nv-hostmgr debug now. also toggled kernel boot param `pcie_aspm=off` as a quick test on one node. will report.
maria: quick check: affected nodes all SKUs with NVLINK-enabled interconnect and 48GB GPUs, appears correlated with interconnect firmware 1.2.4 that was updated two weeks ago.
cameron: @devon can you correlate reset spikes with batch size or steady-state traffic? maybe a workload trigger.
devon: looked at request traces — spikes line up with large tensor broadcast patterns (massive all-reduce) from a nightly eval job. we queued a duplicate run on a non-canary pool (older driver 535) — no resets.
isabel: that suggests a driver/kernel/firmware interaction when NVLINK+all-reduce occurs. steps: 1) keep canary paused, 2) rollback driver on canary hosts to 535.x, 3) capture full 'perf record' around a repro, 4) create incident with vendor.
ops-bot: (runbook) Incident template prefilled: severity=high, impact=canary throughput degraded, mitigation=rollback, owner=@cameron.
cameron: kicking rollback now for the 6 affected nodes. will attach the rollback job id once started.
maria: also creating a short alert refinement: split the existing 'gpu-reset' alert into two — 'reset-with-nvlink' and 'reset-generic' so we can target escalation. thoughts?
devon: +1. current alert is too noisy. having the NVLINK-specific filter (look for nvlink or pci link errors in kernel logs) will help routing to infra vs runtime.
isabel: vendor (NVIDIA) wants: - full dmesg, - nv-hostmgr logs, - firmware versions, - nvidia-smi -q, - reproducer timeline. I'm prepping an upload to the support portal.
cameron: one immediate mitigation that helped in a single test node was disabling ASPM and reducing PCIe link speed to GEN3 via setpci — not ideal cluster-wide but confirms a link-layer sensitivity.
devon: good to note in runbook: 1) pause rollout, 2) isolate nodes with NVLINK, 3) lower PCIe link speed / disable ASPM as temporary, 4) rollback driver if reproduces, 5) vendor engagement.
maria: I'll update the runbook doc and the oncall checklist. Also adding a metric: fraction of resets that co-occur with 'NVLINK' or 'pci_bus_error' so we can fine-grain alerts.
cameron: rollback job id: rollback-1759991234-01 started at 09:52 UTC. ops-scheduler shows nodes reimaged to driver 535.86.
devon: after rollback the three repro nodes ran the same all-reduce workload for 30m with zero resets. solid signal.
isabel: filing support ticket with vendor now, attaching logs + reproducer steps. tagging @maria for runbook updates.
ops-bot: (automated) Alert rule created: 'gpu_reset_nvlink' -> query logs for keywords [nvlink, pci_bus_error, Uncorrected] and high-reset-rate; route to eng-infra.
cameron: thanks everyone. follow-up: we'll hold kernel/driver upgrades for NVLINK SKUs until vendor response and a firmware/driver combo test pass.
devon: leaving this thread open for postmortem notes; will add mitigation timestamps and rollback metrics to the incident doc.
__notes: generated slack thread for infra GPU driver/kernel regression monitoring and runbook activity
